regions.text: reincnVerstandes）と云つてゐる。この種の偶然性に開して「範職の純粋な意味において偶然であるのは、その矛盾営が可能なものである」と云つてゐる。

quote.translation: "Intelligible contingency" Kant also calls "contingency according to concepts of the pure understanding" (Zufälligkeit nach Begriffen des reinen Verstandes), and of this kind of contingency he says that "what is contingent in the pure sense of the category is that whose contradictory opposite is possible".

regions.text: 「運動が在つたのと同じ時間に於て運動の代りに静止が在り得た』如き場合が可想偶然である。

quote.translation: A case in which "at the same time as there was motion, there could have been rest in place of motion" is intelligible contingency: when A exists, the case in which it is also possible that non-A exists in place of A is intelligible contingency.

regions.text: すなはち離接地平に於ける形而上彼然を可想前偶然と云つてるる。

quote.translation: That is to say, Kant calls metaphysical contingency on the disjunctive horizon intelligible contingency.

regions.text: 邏験的偶然を可想的偶然との差異は反對が知む脚に可能である場合と剛脚に可能である場合との相遂であると云つてもよい。

quote.translation: The difference between empirical contingency and intelligible contingency may be said to be the difference between the case in which the opposite is possible successively and the case in which it is possible simultaneously.

regions.text: さうしてカントは經驗偶然性から可想偶然性へ移るここは「他の種類への樽移」（AETBucessisaANoNevos）して全然不可能であると云つてるる（1），B3.456-188）批判主義の立場で現象界の認識に限局される限りこの一種の偶然性を腰別して一方から他坊への推移を不可能をするのは當然のことと云へる。

quote.translation: Kant holds that to move from empirical contingency to intelligible contingency is wholly impossible, being "a transition to another kind" (μετάβασις εἰς ἄλλο γένος) (Ib., B. 486-488), and insofar as one is confined, at the critical standpoint, to knowledge of the world of appearances, it can be said to be natural to distinguish sharply between these two kinds of contingency and to rule out any passage from the one to the other.

regions.text: 然しながら経驗約圏果必然を離接に偶然化して形而上約偶然と見ることすなはち大元の樽化によって羅驗的偶然を可想約偶然とを根柢に於て同一のものと見ることは形而上學的地平に立つ限りば許さるべきことでなければならぬ。カ

quote.translation: Yet to make empirical causal necessity disjunctively contingent and see it as metaphysical contingency, that is, through a conversion of dimension to see "empirical contingency" and "intelligible contingency" as one and the same at the root, must be permitted insofar as one stands on the metaphysical horizon.
